title: Storage and persistence
summary: Key-value storage, secure storage for secrets, databases for structured data, and versioned, cached reads and writes.

sections.title: Choosing storage
sections.body:
- **Async key-value storage**: simple string values, asynchronous, unencrypted. Good for preferences and small caches.
- **Secure storage**: the iOS Keychain or Android Keystore-backed storage, for tokens and secrets. Never put tokens in plain key-value storage.
- **SQLite or another embedded database**: structured or large data, queries and offline-first apps.
- **Synchronous key-value stores** built on JSI: fast reads for settings needed at startup.
- **Files**: images and downloads, in the app's document or cache directory.

sections.title: Values are strings
sections.body: Key-value storage stores strings, so you `JSON.stringify` on write and `JSON.parse` on read. Parsing can fail on corrupt or old data, so wrap it and fall back to a default. Every call is async and crosses to native code, so cache hot values in memory and batch writes with multi-get and multi-set where available.

sections.title: Versioning and migrations
sections.body: Stored data outlives app versions. Save a version number with the data and migrate old shapes when you read them, rather than crashing on a missing field. Users skip versions, so run migrations step by step from the stored version to the current one.

sections.title: Practising it here
sections.body: Exercises here run as TypeScript in a browser sandbox with no React Native runtime, so they model this logic as plain functions and reducers. The same functions drop straight into a real app: call them from a component, a hook or a store. The exercise takes an injected async storage object, so it can be tested with an in-memory fake.

pitfalls: Storing auth tokens in unencrypted key-value storage.
Calling `JSON.parse` on stored data without a try/catch.
Reading storage on every render instead of once with an in-memory cache.
Changing a stored shape without a version or migration.

gotchas.question: Is async key-value storage encrypted?
gotchas.answer: No. It is plain storage in the app sandbox. Use the Keychain or Keystore through a secure storage module for secrets.

gotchas.question: A user updates from version 1 to version 4 of your stored settings. How should migrations run?
gotchas.answer: In order: 1→2, 2→3, 3→4. Each migration only knows the previous shape, so you cannot jump straight to 4.

gotchas.question: Why keep an in-memory cache in front of storage?
gotchas.answer: Every storage call is async and crosses to native code. A cache makes repeated reads instant and lets you write through on change.
